test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.**

Cornelius said to Pauline, “You can have your old job back with a raise in the salary.”

options.text: Cornelius requested Pauline to take her old job back with a raise in the salary.
Cornelius told Pauline that she can have her old job back with a raise in the salary.
Cornelius assured Pauline that she could have her old job back with a raise in the salary.
Cornelius said to Pauline that you can have your old job back with a raise in the salary.

solution:
The correct answer is- 'Cornelius assured Pauline that she could have her old job back with a raise in the salary.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To change the sentence to an indirect speech we need to follow the following steps:

 
 
• As the reported speech shows an *imperative mood*, the reporting speech said to will change to assured.
 
• The inverted commas of reported speech should be replaced with the conjunction '*that*.'
 
• The model verb ***can ***will change to ***could***.
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• Direct: *She said, ‘She **can **dance’.*
 
• Indirect: *She said that she **could **dance.*
 
 
 
 
 
• The pronoun *you *will change to *she *(as it refers to **Pauline**)
 
• The possessive adjective *your *will change to *her.*
 
 
 
• Thus according to the given steps, *option 3 *is the correct answer.

And the correct sentence is: *Cornelius assured Pauline that she could have her old job back with a raise in the salary.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• While changing **direct speech **to **indirect speech**, the **modal verbs **used in the sentences change like:

 
 
• *Can *becomes *could*

 
 
• Direct: *She said, ‘She **can **dance’.*
 
• Indirect: *She said that she **could **dance. *
 
 
 
• *May *becomes *might*
 
 
• Direct: *She said, ‘I **may **buy a dress’.*
 
• Indirect:* She said that she **might **buy a dress.*
 
 
 
• *Must *becomes *had to /would have to* 
 
 
• Direct: *Rama said, ‘I **must **complete the assignment’.*
 
• Indirect: *Rama said that he **had to **complete the assignment.*
 
 
 
• There are modal verbs that do not change – ***Could, Would, Should, Might, Ought to***
 
 
• Direct: *She said, ‘I **should **clean the house.'*
 
• Indirect: *She said that she **should **clean the house.*
